scope: Proposition 9.5 (An odd cube with a bounded even companion) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 70. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed symbols A, A0 just chosen, suppose A(1) = 0. There is a constant C such that, for every sufficiently large b, one can find an odd negative fundamental discriminant k and a finite family hx = Y p (p∗ )fp(x) , x ∈ Fb 2, fp : Fb 2 −→ F2 linear, with the following properties. (i) The primes are distinct good odd primes outside the fixed exclusions; h0 = 1, and every hx has the local squareclasses of 1 at the fixed support and at infinity. Each hx is coprime to k. The field K = Q( √ k) satisfies the standing Heegner conditions. (ii) The prime support of k has cardinality at most C. At every nonroot prime p | Q x hx, the parameter k is a local square. At every nonroot prime q | k, every hx is a local square. (iii) The simultaneous symbol values are A0(|k|) = 1, A(|hx|) = A0(|khx|) = 1 (x ̸= 0). Consequently E(k) has analytic rank zero and s(k) ≤ C. For the odd source, these assertions mean simultaneous actual tests at arbitrarily high admissible precisions after b and its finite set of tests have been fixed. The constant C is independent of b, that precision, and all moving primes. The parameter k may vary with the finite realization.
